statements.answer: Honestly I am mostly here because my partner suggested it. I do not have goals as such — I expect to be told there is nothing to find. No previous assessments, nothing in the family that I know of.
statements.question: What brings you to this assessment now, and is there anything about your background you think is relevant?

statements.answer: No, concentrating is fine for me. I can read a long report or sit through a film without any trouble at all. This has honestly never been an issue in my life.
statements.question: Think about an ordinary day. What is it like for you to stay focused on one thing?

statements.answer: No, organization is not a problem for me. Everything has its place and I keep a tidy calendar. People at work actually comment on it, which always makes me laugh given why I am here.
statements.question: How do you find organizing your time, your tasks, or your belongings?

statements.answer: No, starting tasks is honestly fine for me. Once I decide to do something I just get on with it. I have never really had that problem people talk about where you stare at a task and cannot begin.
statements.question: What kinds of tasks are hardest for you to start or finish?

statements.answer: No, I rarely forget things. Keys, wallet, phone — I always know where they are. My memory is perfectly good, ask anyone who knows me.
statements.question: Do you ever forget appointments, obligations, or where you put things? What is that like?

statements.answer: If I am restless it is the coffee, honestly. I am on about four or five cups on a night shift and then I wonder why I am bouncing my leg. That is a lifestyle thing, not anything else.
statements.question: When you need to sit still or stay with one thing, what is that like for you?

statements.answer: No, I am a patient person. I wait my turn and think before I speak. Nobody who knows me would call me impulsive, I am fairly confident of that.
statements.question: How are you with waiting your turn, or holding back when you want to jump in?

statements.answer: No, nothing was ever flagged at school. Good reports, no complaints, nothing anyone ever raised. There is genuinely nothing to dig up there — I was a boringly normal kid that way.
statements.question: Thinking back to childhood and school, what do you remember about yourself as a child?

statements.answer: No, there is no course to describe, because there has never been a problem. Things have been steady all along — same person at fifteen as at thirty, more or less.

statements.answer: No difference anywhere. Home, work, out with friends — all the same, all fine. I do not have a 'bad setting' because there is nothing going wrong.
statements.question: Are these experiences different depending on where you are — for example at home versus work or study?

statements.answer: No, work is fine, my reviews have always been decent. Nothing is falling through the cracks as far as I can tell, and nobody has ever suggested otherwise. My manager would tell me straight.

statements.answer: No, my relationships are good. No complaints from anyone. We get on well and I am present when it matters — birthdays remembered, promises kept.
